title: Bounded-degree generation of a graded Rees submodule
statement: Let A be a Noetherian commutative ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], I an ideal, and M_n a family of A-modules. Suppose their direct sum has a finite module structure over Rees(I) [def-nagata-rees-algebra], and A-linear maps mu_(k,m)(a): M_m -> M_(m+k) for a in I^k describe its action by coefficient convolution. Let K_n be A-submodules such that mu_(k,m)(a)(K_m) is contained in K_(m+k). Then there is c0 such that each K_n is contained in the A-span of all mu_(k,d)(a)(y), transported along d+k=n, with d<=c0, a in I^k and y in K_d.

source.place: Lemma 02OA, proof of (3), graded-kernel paragraph; independently read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02OA

proof.text: Form the Rees submodule N of the direct sum whose degree-n component belongs to K_n. The convolution formula and closure assumption prove scalar closure degree by degree. Use Noetherianity of the Rees algebra and finiteness of the ambient module to obtain finite generators s of N.

Let c0 bound the union of the supports of s. Each generator is the sum of its homogeneous components, all in K, so N is contained in the Rees span of homogeneous elements of K in degrees at most c0. This also works when s is empty.

For every element x of that span, prove simultaneously for every b in Rees(I) and n that the degree-n component of b*x lies in the stated A-span. Span induction handles sums and scalar multiples (using multiplication of b); on a homogeneous generator the convolution formula leaves precisely terms with d+k=n. Apply this to b=1 and the homogeneous embedding of any element of K_n.

lean.statement:
theorem bounded_generators
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] (I : Ideal A)
    (M : ℕ → Type v) [∀ n, AddCommGroup (M n)] [∀ n, Module A (M n)]
    (mu : ∀ (k m : ℕ) (a : A), a ∈ I ^ k → M m →ₗ[A] M (m + k))
    (mod : Module (reesAlgebra I) (⨁ n : ℕ, M n))
    (hfin : @Module.Finite (reesAlgebra I) (⨁ n : ℕ, M n) _ _ mod)
    (hact : ∀ (b : reesAlgebra I) (x : ⨁ n : ℕ, M n),
      @SMul.smul _ _ mod.toSMul b x =
        ∑ k ∈ b.val.support, ∑ m ∈ x.support,
          DirectSum.of M (m + k) (mu k m (b.val.coeff k) (b.property k) (x m)))
    (K : ∀ n, Submodule A (M n))
    (hK : ∀ (k m : ℕ) (a : A) (ha : a ∈ I ^ k) (y : M m),
      y ∈ K m → mu k m a ha y ∈ K (m + k)) :
    ∃ c0 : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, K n ≤ Submodule.span A
      {z : M n | ∃ (d k : ℕ) (h : d + k = n), d ≤ c0 ∧
        ∃ (a : A) (ha : a ∈ I ^ k) (y : M d),
          y ∈ K d ∧ z = h ▸ mu k d a ha y}
